name: GLARE
ability_definition: The ability to see objects in the presence of a glare or bright lighting.

task_realism.reasoning: Detecting traffic signs in real dashcam footage under heavy sun glare closely matches a core workplace case of this ability: drivers and vehicle operators seeing roadside objects while facing the sun. It does not cover other occupational glare settings, such as pilots, machine operators, welders, reflective surfaces or oncoming headlights.

evaluation_conditions.reasoning: The images are real-world captures, not synthetic, which helps. However, evaluation uses static frames with no temporal continuity, no motion, no time pressure and no consequences for errors. Train and test come from the same distribution. The glare sources are mostly in the sky rather than falling on the target objects, which weakens the stress test compared with real glare that washes out the object itself.

construct_coverage.reasoning: The slice is narrow: one sign per image, 41 US sign classes, one domain (roadway) and one glare source (sun). It covers little of the broader ability, which includes varied objects, artificial light sources, specular reflections, glare adaptation and recovery, and cluttered multi-object scenes.

format_match.reasoning: The inputs are authentic dashcam images, and bounding-box detection scored by mAP is a meaningful perception output for driving-assistance work. It is not a toy format. Still, it stops at localization and labeling rather than the downstream recognition-to-action judgments that real work requires.

transferability_reasoning: GLARE uses real sun-glare driving imagery and object-level detection scoring, so it directly targets seeing objects in bright light in a realistic workplace domain. Its transfer is limited by narrow scope (single sign per image, one domain, sun glare only), static evaluation without real-time or safety stakes, and glare that often falls away from the target objects. Overall it offers moderate evidence for general glare-robust workplace perception.

2023.metric: mAP@0.5:0.95 (percentage points) on the GLARE test set
2023.human_reference: General adult population, specifically typical licensed drivers who must see and identify traffic signs under sun glare

2025.metric: mAP@0.5:0.95 (percentage points) on the GLARE test set
2025.human_reference: General adult drivers with normal vision who recognize traffic signs under sun glare while driving
